A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoDeC research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original contamination-detection results, including Table 1's dataset-level AUC comparisons, finetuning experiments, ablations, and the broader model audit in Table 3.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds token-saliency, paraphrasing, mixed-corpus, adversarial-dataset, and context-selection experiments.

M1.justification: The likelihood comparison, randomly sampled context, sign-based contamination score, and aggregation remain unchanged. Appendix C.8 explicitly presents KNN selection as a diagnostic experiment and retains uniform random sampling for CoDeC.

E1.justification: The original benchmark coverage is retained, but v2 substantially extends tested input conditions: GPT-rephrased MMLU, GSM8K, ArXiv, and Wikipedia; broad training mixtures; and deliberately repetitive, noisy, random-word, and adversarially mixed datasets. These scenarios go beyond the cropping, formatting, and partial-mixture tests already present in v1.

E2.justification: Figure 3 and Table 1 retain the same Vanilla Loss, Min-K%, and Zlib Ratio comparators. Correcting Min-K%'s citation does not change the evaluated method. The new KNN experiments are context-selection ablations rather than an added contamination-detection baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces substantial new experimental designs: probing three GSM8K problems before and after two epochs of Pythia-410M finetuning, sweeping repetition within 128 examples, and comparing random versus nearest-neighbor contexts within and across datasets. The broader audit also adds Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507. These additions do not establish changes to the retained experiments' settings.

E4.justification: Appendices C.2, C.5, C.7, and C.8 add dataset-averaged token-confidence traces, token-saliency case studies, paraphrase and mixed-corpus contamination transfer, duplication sensitivity, adversarial constructions, and context-source/KNN ablations. They investigate mechanism and failure conditions substantially beyond v1's existing analyses.

E5.justification: Section 3.4 adds a Bernoulli-trial framing for deriving confidence bounds, but reports no new calculated bounds. Five-seed averaging, Figure 9's five-run minimum–maximum shading, and the annual-benchmark Wilcoxon tests with FDR correction remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained broad-audit rows are unchanged, but substantial results are added. V2 Table 3 reports 0% for repetitive/noisy/random-word cases and 37–57% for adversarial mixtures. Figure 22 reports random versus KNN scores of 83.7% versus 52.8% for seen Pile and 37.2% versus 0.5% for unseen MMLU. Table 4 adds the Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 results.

T1.justification: The CoDeC score and AUC definitions remain unchanged. V2 adds empirical explanations and a brief confidence-bound suggestion, but no substantive formal derivation, theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain context-based, model-agnostic contamination detection, 99.9% dataset-level AUC, and auditing models with undisclosed training data. V2's emphasis on rephrased data supports v1's existing claim about related and augmented distributions rather than introducing a new central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 substantially develops explanations of selective token reliance after finetuning and the competing effects of helpful context and disrupted memorization. Appendices C.7–C.8 expand the earlier adversarial caveats into discussions of repetition, heterogeneous mixtures, and KNN mitigation, including why similar contexts lower both seen and unseen scores and introduce additional design choices.

D1.justification: V2 adds documented links to a code notebook, project page, and live leaderboard, plus the exact paraphrasing prompt and attention-probe settings. The original implementation disclosures remain intact. The exact GPT version and KNN embedding/similarity settings are still unspecified.

R1.justification: Razeghi et al. (2022) is newly cited in Section 2.2. Most other reference changes consolidate duplicate entries, update publication metadata, or correct attribution, including citing the already-listed Shi et al. (2024) for Min-K%. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and explanatory edits, cleans up references, subdivides Appendix C.2, and moves the broader evaluation from C.7 to Appendix D. Most main-text prose and Appendices A–B retain their original organization and wording.

P2.justification: Figure 10 expands from two examples to four panels including dataset averages. V2 adds saliency maps, transfer curves, repetition and context-distribution plots, KNN comparisons, and an adversarial-results table. Existing displays are largely retained or relocated, while the broad-audit table and ranking charts incorporate the additional model.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for existing claims through paraphrase and mixed-corpus tests and makes previously qualitative adversarial caveats empirically assessable. The code-notebook link and paraphrasing prompt also improve reproducibility information. These are useful gains, although the mechanistic evidence remains illustrative and important GPT/KNN settings are unspecified; the additions do not resolve the paper's outstanding theoretical and interpretive limitations.
